worst average performance of the year

for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) over the past decade. The seasonal setup does not guarantee another selloff, but it raises the risk that any negative catalyst could hit harder as investors move beyond August's historically stronger backdrop.

Recent history also shows the seasonal pattern can be broken. SPY gained

and
3.3% in September 2025
, snapping a multi-year run of losses.
That leaves investors facing a familiar question: whether 2026 will mark a return to September weakness or another year in which strong market momentum overwhelms seasonality.
Investor Takeaway
Investors should treat September seasonality as a risk indicator rather than a standalone sell signal.
The
second half of the month

deserves particular attention given its historically weak record. Investors should also watch whether market breadth deteriorates, volatility rises or major indexes begin losing key technical support.

A resilient first half followed by continued earnings strength could weaken the bearish seasonal case. But if selling pressure begins building alongside negative economic, interest-rate or earnings developments, September's historical tendency toward sharper late-month declines could quickly become more relevant.

title: S&P 500 Faces Its Cruelest Month of the Year
